key_decisions: CPU INinference IS OUT OF SCOPE. The user ruled 2026-07-31 that it is a fallback essentially nobody uses. Do not spend effort on CPU-only defects, do not pin kornia_rs, do not add a CPU preflight, and do NOT publish a hardware/ISA requirement on the docs site (the floor was never confirmed - objdump is not on the box).

MPI-198's proof needs NO download and NO compute: isCompleteOnDisk (routes/downloadCompletion.js:16-18) is EXISTENCE-ONLY, and ComfyUI validates value_not_in_list at /prompt BEFORE reading any weight. Four zero-byte .safetensors make the app treat a model as installed; a 200 + prompt_id is the proof. Wan 2.2 5B was chosen for needing the FEWEST files (4 vs Klein 15 vs Krea 2 ~19). DELETE the placeholders afterwards - install state is existence-only, so the app believes the model is installed forever until they go.

A SINGLE-FILE SWAP FROM THE OFFICIAL TARBALL is a legitimate way to test a server-code fix without a 503MB transfer and an 8GB engine rebuild. Extract the member with `tar -xzf <tgz> --strip-components=2 <path>`, then DIFF it against the box's copy first - if the diff is exactly the fix, the test is a clean isolation. Verified twice this session.
GNU tar reads 'D:/...' as a REMOTE HOST ('Cannot connect to D: resolve failed'). Use the POSIX form '/d/...'.

`pkill -f <pattern>` over SSH KILLS ITS OWN SESSION when the pattern appears in the remote command line - exit 255, and it looks like a connection failure. Bit twice this session. Use a pattern that cannot match the command, or accept the 255 and re-check state separately.
The Linux box has NO curl and NO objdump. Use engine/comfy-venv/bin/python3 with urllib.

Server-code fixes can be driven ENTIRELY over SSH via HTTP (POST /engine/download, POST /comfy/start, GET /comfy/status) - no UI click needed. Only RENDERER-code fixes (like MPI-198's heal) need the user to click, because the op strip ignores synthetic clicks.

PEP 440: a version with a local segment (2.13.0+cpu) OUTRANKS the same version without one (2.13.0). This is why --upgrade could never have replaced the CPU torch with PyPI's build, and it is what disproved MPI-413.

PyPI's linux `torch` wheel IS the CUDA build - it declares the nvidia-* dependencies. So a node requirements install that resolves bare `torch` on a box with no torch present pulls the whole CUDA stack. That, not --upgrade, is where MPI-413's evidence came from.
